title: VFQ DXP — User Journey to Access Control Process Flow
subtitle: Traceability model rendered as process: User Journey → Workflow/Task → View → Action → Access/Permission. Type mapping — Journey = cyan terminal, Workflow/Task = violet (orchestrated), View = emerald (human-in-loop screen), Action = amber (operation invoked against the platform), Access/Permission = rose gate.
footer: Vodafone Qatar DXP • Journey–Workflow–View–Action–Permission traceability • representative model, see provenance note

flow.title: Journey Selection
flow.meaning: The entry workflow resolves which of the four modelled journeys the customer is on (UJ-001 Prepaid Activation, UJ-002 Postpaid Activation, UJ-003 FWA Activation, UJ-004 SIM Swap) and which channel the agent is working in (Desktop, Tablet, Vanilla, Open UI). Every downstream view, action and permission is selected from this resolution.
flow.inputDesc: Journey entry point, channel, agent session
flow.outputDesc: Resolved journey variant, channel-specific view set
flow.example: A sales rep on a tablet starts a new postpaid activation; routing selects UJ-002 and the Open UI Tablet view set.

flow.title: Activation Form
flow.meaning: The channel-appropriate data-entry surface. VW-001 (Prepaid Activation Form) captures customer and service selection; VW-002 (Postpaid Activation Form) extends it with the fields the credit evaluation needs.
flow.inputDesc: Resolved journey variant, channel view set
flow.example: Agent keys name, contact and plan into the Open UI Tablet postpaid form.

title: Sales Agent
Access?
flow.meaning: AP-001 (Sales Agent Access) governs creating and editing orders on tablet and desktop. Authorisation is resolved before the session may query the customer master or commit anything — without it the form is readable but inert.
flow.example: A read-only analytics user (AP-007) can open the form but is refused at this gate.

flow.title: Search Customer
flow.meaning: AC-018 queries the CRM master so an existing customer is reused rather than duplicated. This is the action that makes the journey idempotent against the customer master. Requires AP-001.
flow.inputDesc: Identifier entered on the activation form
flow.outputDesc: Matched customer record or a new-customer flag
flow.example: QID lookup returns an existing account, so the journey continues against that customer rather than creating a second one.

flow.title: Validate Identity
flow.meaning: WF-001 orchestrates identity validation. It is a precondition for WF-002 eligibility and, for postpaid, for WF-003 credit assessment — no order reaches approval without it.
flow.example: Postpaid activation requires QID plus a bank document; the workflow raises both as outstanding items.

flow.title: Document Upload
flow.meaning: VW-004 is the shared upload surface reused by every journey that needs proof of identity or means of payment. It is reached from both VW-001 and VW-002, and it is where rejected documents are replaced.
flow.example: Agent photographs the customer's QID on the tablet and attaches a bank statement PDF.

flow.title: Upload Document
flow.meaning: AC-003 performs the transfer and binds each artefact to the order. It always precedes AC-004 verification. Requires AP-001.
flow.outputDesc: Stored artefact references on the order
flow.example: Two files stored and linked to the draft postpaid order.

flow.title: Verify Document
flow.meaning: AC-004 runs automated verification on the stored artefacts. It is governed by AP-003 (Compliance Verification) — the agent uploads, but the compliance capability decides whether the artefact stands.
flow.example: OCR reads the QID number and expiry; an expired document fails here rather than at approval.

title: Documents
Valid?
flow.meaning: The validation gate, governed by AP-003. A failure returns the agent to VW-004 to replace the rejected artefact rather than terminating the journey — this is the most frequently exercised alternate path in the model.
flow.example: An expired passport is rejected; the agent is returned to the upload view to capture a current one.

flow.title: Check Eligibility
flow.meaning: WF-002 resolves the customer segment and the rules that follow from it. Segment is what makes the journey branch: HRN and postpaid carry a credit assessment that prepaid does not.
flow.example: Customer resolves to HRN, so a credit limit must be established before the order can be submitted.

title: Credit Check
Required?
flow.meaning: The segment branch. Postpaid and HRN journeys require WF-003 credit assessment; prepaid journeys bypass it entirely and rejoin the process at consent capture. Both paths are live — this is a legitimate alternate route, not an error branch.
flow.example: UJ-001 Prepaid Activation skips straight to signature; UJ-002 Postpaid Activation continues into credit assessment.

flow.title: Calculate Credit
flow.meaning: WF-003 establishes the credit limit that governs what the customer may be sold. It sits between WF-001 identity validation and WF-004 approval submission.
flow.example: HRN customer's bank documents and segment feed a limit request.

flow.title: Score Credit
flow.meaning: AC-006 invokes the credit engine. Governed by AP-004 (Credit Assessment Rights) — the scoring detail is visible only to holders of that permission.
flow.outputDesc: Credit score, assigned limit, risk band
flow.example: Engine returns a limit that caps the device subsidy the agent can offer.

flow.title: Credit Summary
flow.meaning: VW-003 surfaces the calculated limit and its status. It is the view where a credit analyst intervenes if the automated band needs override.
flow.outputDesc: Confirmed credit position on the order
flow.example: Panel shows an approved limit; the agent proceeds to configure the plan within it.

title: Credit Assessment
Rights?
flow.meaning: AP-004 gates access to scoring detail and limit assignment. A sales agent without it cannot see or alter the band — the case is referred to the credit team rather than blocking the customer.
flow.example: Tablet sales rep sees only the approved/declined outcome; the numeric band is withheld and the case referred.

flow.title: Capture Consent
flow.meaning: WF-008 is the rejoin point for both branches — prepaid arrives here directly from the segment gate, postpaid arrives after credit assessment. Consent is captured once, whatever the path.
flow.inputDesc: Configured order (with credit position where applicable)
flow.outputDesc: Consent request bound to the order
flow.example: Both a prepaid SIM sale and a postpaid contract converge on the same consent step.

flow.title: Signature Capture
flow.meaning: VW-005 is the tablet/mobile surface where the customer signs. Reused unchanged across every journey that needs consent.
flow.example: Customer signs on the tablet in front of the agent.

flow.title: Store Signature
flow.meaning: AC-005 encrypts the signature and binds it to the order. It is always followed by AC-014 audit logging — consent is an auditable event.
flow.outputDesc: Encrypted signature artefact on the order
flow.example: Signature stored against the order id and written to the audit log.

flow.title: Order Summary
flow.meaning: VW-008 is the last point at which the order can be amended by the agent (AC-017 Modify Order). Rejected orders return here to be corrected and resubmitted.
flow.example: Agent and customer review plan, add-ons and charges before submitting.

flow.title: Submit to Queue
flow.meaning: AC-007 hands the order off from the sales channel to the approval workflow. This is the primary handoff in the process — ownership moves from agent to approver.
flow.example: Order leaves the tablet session and appears in the manager's desktop queue.

flow.title: Route for Approval
flow.meaning: WF-004 assigns the queued order to the right approver based on segment and value. B2B2C and HRN orders route differently from standard ones.
flow.example: A B2B2C postpaid order is routed to the partner-approval queue rather than the standard one.

flow.title: Approval Queue
flow.meaning: VW-006 is the approver's working surface — the queue of orders assigned to them. Shared across all journeys; SIM Swap approvals appear in the same queue as activations.
flow.example: Manager opens the desktop queue and picks the oldest pending order.

title: Manager Approval
Rights?
flow.meaning: AP-002 (Manager Approval Rights) governs approve and reject. Where the order exceeds the approver's authority, AP-008 (Escalation Rights) carries it to senior management rather than leaving it stalled.
flow.example: An order above the manager's value threshold escalates instead of being approved.

flow.title: Approval Detail
flow.meaning: VW-009 gives the approver everything the decision needs in one place: the order, the verified documents from VW-004 and the credit position from VW-003.
flow.example: Manager inspects the QID scan and the credit band before deciding.

flow.title: Retrieve Details
flow.meaning: AC-008 assembles the full case for the approver, including prior audit history from AC-014. Governed by AP-002.
flow.example: Retrieval surfaces that this customer had a prior order rejected for document quality.

title: Approve
Order?
flow.meaning: The approval gate. AC-009 approves and triggers activation; AC-010 rejects and opens VW-010 (Rejection Reason Form) to capture why. Both outcomes are audit-logged via AC-014.
flow.example: Manager rejects for an illegible bank document, records the reason, and the order returns to the agent to amend.

flow.title: Activate Service
flow.meaning: WF-006 is the handoff from approval to provisioning. It is the point at which the order becomes a commitment to deliver service.
flow.example: Approved postpaid order is passed to the Vanilla backend for activation.

flow.title: Provision Service
flow.meaning: AC-011 executes the activation. Governed by AP-006 (Administrator Full Access) — no channel user invokes it directly; the workflow does, under system authority.
flow.example: Number provisioned and plan attached on the network.

flow.title: Check Inventory
flow.meaning: AC-023 checks physical stock where the journey needs hardware — a SIM for mobile journeys, CPE for FWA. Governed by AP-009 (Fulfilment Operations).
flow.outputDesc: Stock position for the required item
flow.example: FWA order checks outdoor CPE stock at the serving warehouse.

title: Stock
Available?
flow.meaning: The fulfilment gate. Where stock is short the order is backordered rather than failed — the service activation already succeeded, only the hardware delivery is deferred.
flow.example: Outdoor CPE out of stock: a backorder is raised and the customer is given a revised date.

flow.title: Schedule Delivery
flow.meaning: AC-024 books the delivery, or for FWA outdoor the WFM installation visit. Governed by AP-009 (Fulfilment Operations).
flow.outputDesc: Delivery booking or WFM work order
flow.example: FWA outdoor installation booked as a WFM engineer visit rather than a courier drop.

flow.title: Notify Customer
flow.meaning: WF-007 composes what the customer is told: what was activated, when hardware arrives, and how to track it.
flow.example: Confirmation combines the activated plan with the booked installation window.

flow.title: Send Confirmation
flow.meaning: AC-012 (SMS) and AC-013 (Email) dispatch the notification. Both are logged to the audit trail by AC-014.
flow.outputDesc: Delivered SMS and email, delivery receipts
flow.example: Customer receives an SMS with the activation confirmation and an email with the full service summary.

flow.title: Status Tracker
flow.meaning: VW-011 is the only customer-facing view in the model. Governed by AP-005 (Customer Self-Service Access), which also permits AC-019 order history and AC-020 invoice download.
flow.inputDesc: Delivered notice, activation and delivery state
flow.example: Customer follows the CPE shipment (AC-025) through to the installation slot.

flow.title: Write Audit Trail
flow.meaning: AC-014 records the whole journey — validations, approvals, rejections, notifications. Read access is governed by AP-010 (Audit Trail Access), and it is the evidence base for AC-015 reporting under AP-007.
flow.inputDesc: Events emitted across every prior step
flow.outputDesc: Immutable audit record for the journey
flow.example: Compliance reconstructs who approved an order, when, and against which documents.

loops.label: VW-010 reason → AC-017 amend
loops.meaning: A rejected order is not a dead end. The approver records a reason in VW-010 (Rejection Reason Form) and the order returns to the agent at VW-008 (Order Summary), where AC-017 Modify Order applies the correction before resubmission.

loops.label: service change / UJ-004 SIM Swap re-enters journey
loops.meaning: An active customer re-entering the estate — a SIM swap (UJ-004), a plan change, or a home move — starts the same journey selection workflow again against the existing record rather than a new one. This is what makes the model a lifecycle rather than a one-shot activation.

ioTable.input: Journey entry point, channel, agent session
ioTable.output: Resolved journey variant, channel-specific view set
ioTable.example: Tablet postpaid start → UJ-002 + Open UI Tablet views
ioTable.meaning: Journey selection resolves which of the four journeys and which channel is in play; every downstream view, action and permission follows from this. Gated by AP-001 before any customer data is queried.

ioTable.input: Customer record, QID / Passport / Bank documents
ioTable.meaning: WF-001 identity validation runs through VW-004 upload and AC-003/AC-004 verification, gated by AP-003 Compliance Verification. Failures return to the upload view rather than ending the journey.

ioTable.output: Eligibility verdict, credit limit and band
ioTable.example: HRN segment → credit limit assigned by AC-006
ioTable.meaning: WF-002 resolves segment and branches: postpaid and HRN take WF-003 credit assessment under AP-004; prepaid bypasses it and rejoins at consent capture.

ioTable.output: Signed order in the approval queue
ioTable.example: Tablet signature → encrypted artefact → queued order
ioTable.meaning: WF-008 captures consent through VW-005 and AC-005, VW-008 gives the last amendment point, and AC-007 hands ownership from the sales channel to the approver.

ioTable.example: AC-009 approve, or AC-010 reject with VW-010 reason
ioTable.meaning: WF-004 assigns the queue, VW-006 and VW-009 present the case, and AP-002 governs the decision — with AP-008 escalation where the order exceeds the approver's authority.

ioTable.output: Activated service, delivery or WFM booking
ioTable.example: FWA outdoor → CPE allocated → engineer visit booked
ioTable.meaning: WF-006 provisions through AC-011 under AP-006, then AC-023 and AC-024 handle stock and delivery under AP-009. Short stock backorders rather than fails.

ioTable.output: Customer notification, tracked status, audit record
ioTable.example: SMS + email sent; customer tracks CPE shipment
ioTable.meaning: WF-007 and AC-012/AC-013 notify, VW-011 gives the customer self-service visibility under AP-005, and AC-014 writes the immutable trail read under AP-010.
